name: Ascento Guard
description: A two-wheeled, self-balancing patrol robot from Ascento (an ETH Zurich spin-off) with spring-like "wheel-leg" hybrid legs that let it climb curbs, stairs, and rough terrain. Sold only as B2B robot-as-a-service, not to consumers.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: Ascento Research / The Robot Report; ranges 30–32 kg across sources

specs.label: Height
specs.note: variable — crouches/extends via wheel-leg suspension; ~70 × 50 cm footprint

specs.label: Business Model
specs.note: hourly rental, not sold as hardware

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: remote human alert triage included in the hourly rental — no separate monitoring tier

sourcing: Verified against Ascento's own official site (ascento.ai), TechCrunch and Forbes launch coverage, and The Robot Report's Guard and Guard 2.0 coverage. Company funding/status information is only confirmed through 2024 reporting; no 2025–2026 update was found. "Watchlist" could not be confirmed as an Ascento product or customer name and should not be treated as accurate. Do not confuse this B2B "Ascento Guard" security robot with "Ascento Pro," a similarly-descended but separately-sold research/education robot from a different company (MYBOTSHOP).

pricing.summary: Ascento Guard is not sold as a purchasable product with a listed MSRP — it's leased through a robot-as-a-service model at an hourly rate to business customers, with pricing arranged per contract rather than published publicly.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: Ascento Guard (Guard 2.0) uses a wheel-leg hybrid: variable-length, spring-like legs on a two-wheel-drive base let it self-balance, self-right, and crouch or extend to climb curbs, stairs, and rough or snowy terrain, its defining feature versus flat-ground-only patrol robots. Caution: no evidence 'Watchlist' is an Ascento product; don't confuse Guard with the separately-made 'Ascento Pro' education robot.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: The name "Watchlist," sometimes associated with Ascento, is not an actual Ascento product or confirmed customer. Ascento Guard should also not be confused with "Ascento Pro," a similarly-descended but separately-sold research/education robot from a different company (MYBOTSHOP).

firmwareCommunity.note: Ascento Robotics has not released a public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API for Guard. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
